chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Zakariyya ibn Adam said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) when he enters [the state of Ihram] on the Day of Arafah. He said: 'There is no Tamattu' for him; he makes it a separate Umrah.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mutamatti' enters Ihram for Hajj on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal consequence of delaying the transition from Umrah to Hajr for a Mutamatti', ruling that the Umrah becomes a standalone act rather than part of the combined ritual. This establishes the critical importance of timely intention (niyyah) and entry into Ihram for Hajj on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah to maintain the validity of the Tamattu' structure. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the temporal link between the two rites is essential for the specific dispensations associated with Hajj al-Tamattu'.
